ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.claim: The prophet narratives share a refrain of God's peace and mercy, support for the messenger's mission, and reward for good deeds; this refrain summarizes the anecdotes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.anchor: It is this motif which, in fact, is the summary of these anecdotes as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.claim: Through Aaron, the prophets are listed chronologically; afterward their order follows each prophet's attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.anchor: Till the mention of Aaron (sws) all prophets are cited in the chronological order; after that the sequence is based on the attributes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.claim: The tasbīḥ here is Jonah’s confession and plea for forgiveness in the words of 21:87, and it brought his deliverance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.anchor: it refers to chanting of the words

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.claim: As soon as the calamity struck, Jonah understood it as punishment and turned to God wholeheartedly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.anchor: as soon as this calamity struck Jonah (sws) it became evident to him that he had been punished by the Almighty and he turned to God with all his heart.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.claim: Jonah’s prayer is described as the best expression of confessing sin and seeking forgiveness from God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.anchor: These are the best of words which express confession of a sin and seeking of forgiveness from God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.claim: The account omits events before the ship and before Jonah's prayer in the darkness; combining this telling with the one in al-Anbiya fills the gaps.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.anchor: ففي قصة يونس عليه السلام هنا جمل محذوفة مقدرة قبل ذكر فراره إلى الفلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r9.claim: Being among those who glorify God means remembering and declaring Him holy; the apparent reference is Jonah's prayer in the darkness in al-Anbiya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r9.anchor: من الذاكرين الله تعالى بالتسبيح والتقديس. والظاهر أنه يريد ما ذكر في قوله في سورة الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r10.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r10.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the glorification was Jonah's utterance Subhan Allah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r10.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: هو قوله سبحان الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r11.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r11.claim: Another group identifies Jonah's glorification as voluntary prayer, with its supporting reports continued in the next segment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة: تسبيحه صلاة التطوع فقال ابن عباس، وقتادة، وأبو العالية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، وأبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r1.claim: They say Jonah's prayer in ease benefited him in distress; al-Dahhak similarly urges remembering God in prosperity so He remembers one in hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r1.anchor: صلاته في وقت الرخاء تنفعه في وقت الشدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the glorification was Jonah's prayer inside the whale.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: تسبيحه: صلاته في بطن الحوت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r3.speaker: روي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r3.claim: One report says Jonah promised the whale he would build a mosque where none had been built before.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r3.anchor: وروي أنه كان يرفع لحم الحوت بيديه يقول: لأبنين لك مسجدا حيث لم يبنه أحد قبلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r4.speaker: روي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r4.claim: Another report says the whale traveled with the ship while Jonah praised God, carried him to shore, and released him unharmed; the people then embraced Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r4.anchor: وروي أن الحوت سافر مع السفينة رافعا رأسه ليتنفس ويونس يسبح

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n57/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n57/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n57/r1.claim: Jonah's being among those who glorify God means remembering God and repenting; his story has universal purport.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n57/r1.anchor: I.e., to remember God and to repent: see 21:87, which reveals in its very formulation the universal purport of Jonah's story.

NASHR:v1p91/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p91/r1.claim: The author confirms the chain for his ten-reading recitation: Ibn al-Qaṣṣāʿ reliably reported that ʿAlī ibn Shujāʿ read al-Miṣbāḥ with al-Ghaznawī, whom he met and heard.
NASHR:v1p91/r1.anchor: وابن القصاع ثقة عارف ضابط، وقد رحل إليه، وقرأ عليه فلولا أنه أخبره بذلك لم يذكره

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r1.claim: Qatada explains the people who glorify God as people who pray.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين ﴾ قال من المصلين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains the people who glorify God as people who pray.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r2.anchor: الثوري عن عاصم عن أبي رزين عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين ﴾ قال من المصلين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r3.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r3.claim: Tawus reports that when Jonah was cast out sick, a gourd grew over him; when it withered he wept, and God asked why he mourned one plant but not the destruction of a hundred thousand people.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r3.anchor: عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه قال بلغني أنه لما نبذه الحوت بالعراء وهو سقيم نبتت عليه شجرة من يقطين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r4.claim: The Prophet says no one should claim to be better than Jonah ibn Matta: Jonah committed a fault, then his Lord chose him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا ينبغي لأحد أن يقول إني خير من يونس بن متى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r5.claim: Qatada transmits a saying of wisdom: good works raise their doer, and whenever he stumbles he finds support.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة بلغني أنه يقال إن في الحكمة العمل الصالح يرفع صاحبه كلما عثر وجد متكأ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Jonah remained in the whale’s belly for forty mornings.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال بلغني أن يونس مكث في بطن الحوت أربعين صباحا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r7.speaker: وهب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r7.claim: Wahb glosses the people who glorify God as worshippers and refers to Jonah’s worship.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r7.anchor: المنذر بن النعمان عن وهب في قوله ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين ﴾ قال من العابدين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r8.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said Jonah heard the earth glorifying God in the whale’s depths; his plea from the darknesses (21:87) was recognized by angels, who asked God to answer his prayer from prosperity, and God ordered the whale to release him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r8.anchor: يحيى بن العلاء قال أخبرني حميد بن صخر عن أنس بن مالك قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما ألقى يونس نفسه في البحر فالتقمه الحوت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the whale left Jonah at the root of a gourd; a female gazelle came morning and evening and gave him milk until his flesh returned.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p155/r9.anchor: فحدثني يزيد بن عبد الله بن قسيط عن أبي هريرة أنه لفظه حين لفظه في أصل يقطينة وهي الدباء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r1.claim: Jonah was among those who remembered God abundantly through glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r1.anchor: أي من الذاكرين الله تعالى كثيرا بالتسبيح كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r2.claim: Qatada's wording suggests that the phrase entails abundant glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r2.anchor: وفي كلام قتادة ما يشعر باعتباره الكثرة واستفادتها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r3.claim: Khafaji says the plural phrase, unlike simply calling him a glorifier, marks Jonah as deeply rooted among them and so implies abundance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r3.anchor: على ما قال الخفاجي من جعله من المسبحين دون أن يقال مسبحا فإنه يشعر بأنه عريق فيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r4.claim: Deriving frequency from the intensive verbal form is challenged: glorification itself need not imply repetition, as in saying Subḥān Allāh.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r4.anchor: ورد بأن معنى سبح لم يعتبر فيه ذلك إذ هو قال سبحانه الله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r5.claim: The definite plural may instead indicate an established habit, since being counted among the glorifiers suggests constancy.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r5.anchor: وقد يقال : هي من إرادة الثبوت من ( المسبحين ) فإنه يشعر بأن التسبيح ديدن لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr takes tasbīḥ in its proper sense: the stated glorification or words equivalent to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r6.anchor: والمراد بالتسبيح ههنا حقيقته وهو القول المذكور أو ما في معناه وروي ذلك عن ابن جبير

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r7.claim: Some place Jonah's being a glorifier before the whale swallowed him, during his time of ease.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r7.anchor: وهذا الكون عند بعض قبل التقام الحوت إياه أيام الرخاء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān locates the glorification inside the whale and identifies it with Jonah's invocation in the darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r8.anchor: واستظهر أبو حيان أنه في بطن الحوت وأن التسبيح ما ذكره الله تعالى في قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r9.claim: Other interpreters understand the phrase as remembrance in general.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r10.speaker: بعض آخر
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r10.claim: Another group understands it as worship in general.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets glorification as prayer and is reported to say that every Quranic occurrence of tasbīḥ means prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r11.anchor: وجماعة منهم ابن عباس على الصلاة بل روي عنه أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that a legal or technical sense of tasbīḥ needs no contextual clue only if it is the sole such established sense; figurative or competing technical senses require a clue.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r12.anchor: إن كان اللفظ فيما ذكر حقيقة شرعية ولم يكن للتسبيح حقيقة أخرى شرعية أيضا لم يحتج إلى قرينة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r13.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r13.claim: Ibn Jubayr says Jonah had prayed before entering the whale.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r13.anchor: عن ابن جبير في قوله تعالى : ( فلو لا أنه كان من المسبحين ) قال : من المصلين قبل أن يدخل بطن الحوت

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r14.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the prayer was one Jonah performed inside the whale; Qatāda rejects this and says it was his prior practice in ease.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r14.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية قال : ما كان إلا صلاة أحدثها في بطن الحوت فذكر ذلك لقتادة فقال : لا إنما كان يعمل في الرخاء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r15.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r15.claim: In another report, al-Ḥasan says Jonah prayed often in ease, feared death in the whale, moved his legs, then prostrated and called the place a sanctuary where none had prostrated before.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144/r15.anchor: كان يكثر الصلاة في الرخاء فلما حصل في بطن الحوت ظن أنه الموت فحرك رجليه فإذا هي تتحرك فسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abī Shayba transmits Dhahhāk b. Qays's admonition to remember God in ease so He remembers one in hardship, illustrated by Jonah the remembering servant and Pharaoh the heedless tyrant at drowning.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك بن قيس قال : اذكروا الله تعالى في الرخاء يذكركم في الشدة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers that Jonah's being among the glorifiers span both ease and the whale's belly; his practice in each period contributed to his release.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#2/r2.anchor: والأولى حمل زمانه كونه من المسبحين على ما يعم زمان الرخاء وزمان كونه في بطن الحوت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r3.claim: Jonah was among those who remembered God earlier and was frequent in remembrance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r3.anchor: من الذاكرين لله قبل ذلك، وكان كثير الذكر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jonah was among those who prayed.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r5.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r5.claim: Wahb says Jonah was among the worshippers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jonah did not pray inside the fish but had done righteous deeds earlier.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما كانت له صلاة في بطن الحوت ولكنه قدم عملا صالحا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God requited Jonah by showing gratitude for earlier obedience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك: شكر الله تعالى له طاعته القديمة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r8.claim: Another view says Jonah glorified God inside the fish; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identifies this with the prayer in 21:87.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: "فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين" في بطن الحوت. قال سعيد بن جبير: يعني قوله: "لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين"

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r10.claim: Jonah praised God throughout life, or in the fish by reciting the prayer in 21:87; another view means he prayed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r10.anchor: الذاكرين الله كثيرا بالتسبيح مدة عمره، أو في بطن الحوت وهو قوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r11.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r11.claim: An alternative understands “the glorifiers” as people who pray.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r11.anchor: إني كنت من الظلمين [الأنبياء: 87] وقيل من المصلين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r1.claim: In the crisis Jonah became detached from himself and all else, abiding in the oneness of God through glorification; this inward state points to why God saved him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r1.anchor: فتجرد عن نفسه وغيرها تجردا لم يكن لأحد مثل مجموعه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r2.claim: Jonah was innately and habitually given to glorifying God with heart, tongue, and limbs, including prayer, in both ease and hardship because his character matched his created purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r2.anchor: وهو ما يصح إطلاق التسبيح في اللغة عليه من التنزيه بالقلب واللسان والأركان بالصلاة وغيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets Jonah's being among those who glorify God as referring to prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r3.anchor: وحمله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما على الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r6.claim: The passage alludes to the saying about knowing God in ease so He will know one in hardship, and urges remembrance while magnifying its importance.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.claim: Because Jonah remembered God in ease, God remembered and rescued him in hardship; the rescue was an astonishing act of divine greatness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.anchor: ولكنه لما كان ذكارا لله في حال الرخاء ذكرناه في حال الشدة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.speaker: مترجمه
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.claim: The translator's Book of Jonah recounts Jonah's commission to Nineveh and flight by ship, a storm and lot that identify him, his being thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish, and his prayer after three days and nights in its belly.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.anchor: قال مترجمه : نبدأ بمعونة الله وقوته بكتب نبوة يونان بن متى النبي

DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.claim: Tawus says the whale expelled Jonah sick; a gourd grew over him, later withered, and God rebuked him for grieving a plant but not a hundred thousand people.
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.anchor: قال طاوس: بلغني أنه لما نبذه الحوت بالعراء وهو سقيم نبتت عليه شجرة من يقطين

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.claim: Al-Rabiʿ b. Anas explains Jonah’s prior righteous work as the reason for deliverance; the accompanying wisdom says good deeds raise their doer.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس رضي الله عنه في قوله {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: لولا أنه حلاله عمل صالح

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r2.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says Jonah had been among those who prayed before entering the whale.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: من المصلين قبل

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah’s prayer was something he performed only after entering the whale.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r3.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: ما كان إلا صلاة أحدثها

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r4.claim: Qatada rejects al-Hasan’s claim that the prayer began in the whale and says Jonah had worshipped in times of ease.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r4.anchor: فذكر ذلك لقتادة رضي الله عنه فقال: لا إنما كان يعمل في الرخاء

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “those who glorify” as those who pray.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: من المصلين

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r6.claim: Mujahid says Jonah had worshipped God before this ordeal.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: العابدين الله قبل ذلك

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.claim: Saʿid b. Abi al-Hasan says a history of worship and glorification rescued Jonah in distress; he remained in the whale forty days and nights before release and repentance.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي الحسن رضي الله عنه {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: لولا أنه كان له سلف

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r8.claim: Al-Hasan teaches that supplication in ease prepares a person to lean on God in hardship, while earlier evil can still catch up with its doer.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: نعلم والله أن التضرع في الرخاء

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak contrasts Jonah, who remembered God in ease and was rescued, with Pharaoh, who remembered only at drowning; Pharaoh’s late profession was rejected.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه قال: اذكروا الله في الرخاء يذكركم في الشدة فإن يونس عليه السلام

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r1.claim: Al-Hasan reports that Jonah prayed often in ease, thought he was dying in the whale, then moved his legs, found them alive, and prostrated, saying he had made God a place of prostration where none had prayed.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r1.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: كان يكثر الصلاة في الرخاء

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the whale swallowed Jonah at midday and expelled him that evening; he did not spend a night inside it.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: التقمه الحوت ضحى ولفظه عشية ما بات في بطنه

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.claim: Qatada says Jonah prayed often in ease and was saved; otherwise the whale’s belly would have become his grave until Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.anchor: وفي قوله {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: كان كثير الصلاة في الرخاء فنجا

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.claim: Shahr b. Hawshab says God told the whale it was made Jonah’s refuge and mosque, not to consume him.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب رضي الله عنه قال: انطلق يونس عليه السلام مغضبا فركب مع قوم في سفينة

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.claim: Ikrima reports Jonah’s prayer from inside the whale: he lists his confinement and asks what good deed he has to offer; angels recognize his familiar voice in a strange place, and God identifies him as Jonah.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: لما ذهب مغاضبا فكان في بطن الحوت قال من بطن الحوت

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.speaker: حميد بن هلال
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.claim: Hamid says Jonah’s body wasted away in the whale; after he invoked God and was cast ashore, the gourd fed him until his body recovered, then it dried and he wept.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.anchor: فكان يونس في بطن الحوت حتى رق العظم وذهب اللحم والبشر والشعر وكان سقيما

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r1.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says Jonah was among those who prayed before he entered the fish.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله : فلولا انه كان من المسبحين قال : من المصلين قبل ان يدخل بطن الحوت

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah’s prayer was one he first performed inside the fish; Qatada rejects this and says Jonah had prayed in times of ease.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : فلولا انه كان من المسبحين قال : ما كان الا صلاة احدثها في بطن الحوت ، فذكر ذلك لقتادة رضي الله ، عنه فقال : لا . انما كان يعمل في الرخاء

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise glosses the phrase as being among those who pray.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس فلولا انه كان من المسبحين قال : من المصلين

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah, thinking he was dying inside the fish, moved his feet, found they still moved, prostrated, and thanked God for being able to worship where no one else had prayed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : فلولا انه كان من المسبحين قال : كان يكثر الصلاة في الرخاء ، فلما حصل في بطن الحوت ، ظن انه الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r9.claim: Qatada says Jonah prayed much in prosperity and was saved; otherwise the fish’s belly would have been his grave until the Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r9.anchor: و في قوله : فلولا انه كان من المسبحين قال : كان كثير الصلاة في الرخاء ، فنجا للبث في بطنه قال : لصار له بطن الحوت قبرا إلى يوم يبعثون قال : إلى يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r5.claim: Being among the glorifiers refers to Jonah’s prayer in 21:87; God rescued him because of his glorification and repentance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r5.anchor: فأنجاه الله بسبب تسبيحه وتوبته فقذفه الحوت من بطنه إلى البر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r6.claim: The author gives three nights in the fish, while also recording alternatives of one day and night or a few hours.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r6.anchor: بعد أن مكث في جوف الحوت ثلاث ليال ، وقيل : يوما وليلة ، وقيل : بضع ساعات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r7.claim: One reported duration for Jonah’s stay in the fish is one day and one night.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r8.claim: Another reported duration for Jonah’s stay in the fish is a few hours.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.claim: Alongside God's prior decree, Yūnus's glorification is given as the reason for his rescue.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.anchor: وجعل تعالى علة استنقاذه مع القدر السابق تسبيحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj says his glorification was the phrase “Glory be to God” inside the whale.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r10.anchor: فقال ابن جريج هو قوله في بطن الحوت سبحان الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r11.claim: Another group understands the glorification as prayer, including voluntary prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل التسبيح وصلاة التطوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r12.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس وأبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r12.claim: Qatāda, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Abū al-ʿĀliya say Yūnus's prayer in ease benefited him in hardship; a group of scholars shares this view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r12.anchor: فقال قتادة وابن عباس وأبو العالية صلاته في وقت الرخاء نفعته في وقت الشدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r13.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r13.claim: From the pulpit, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays urged people to remember God in ease so He remembers them in distress: Yūnus benefited from prior remembrance, while Pharaoh's late belief as he drowned did not help him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r13.anchor: قال الضحاك بن قيس على منبره اذكروا الله في الرخاء يذكركم في الشدة إن يونس كان عبدا لله ذاكرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r14.claim: Qatāda says a person's deeds raise him when he stumbles, leaving him a support if he falls.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r14.anchor: وقال قتادة في الحكمة: إن العمل يرفع صاحبه إذ عثر فإذا صرع وجد متكئا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r15.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan says Yūnus's glorification was prayer inside the whale.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r15.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: كانت سبحته صلاة في بطن الحوت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r16.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r16.claim: A report says Yūnus lifted whale flesh, vowed to build God a mosque where none had been built, and prayed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r16.anchor: وروي أنه كان يرفع لحم الحوت بيديه ويقول يا رب لأبنين لك مسجدا حيث لم يبنه أحد قبلي ويصلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r17.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r17.claim: Anas reports from the Prophet that Yūnus's cry from the darkness rose to the Throne; angels noted a weak voice from a distant place, God identified it as His servant Yūnus, and answered his call.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r17.anchor: وروى أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يونس حين نادى في الظلمات، ارتفع نداؤه إلى العرش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r1.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jubayr says “one of those who glorify” points to Yūnus's prayer, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن جبير الإشارة بقوله من المسبحين إلى قوله لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say the earlier worshippers were people of prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r1.anchor: أحدها من المصلين قاله ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد ووهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid and Wahb ibn Munabbih say they were worshippers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r2.anchor: والثاني من العابدين قاله مجاهد ووهب بن منبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase refers to Jonah’s supplication: there is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r3.anchor: والثالث قول ﴿ لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين ﴾ الأنبياء 87 قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r4.speaker: عمران القطان عن الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r4.claim: ʿImrān al-Qaṭṭān transmits from al-Ḥasan that this was a prayer Jonah first performed inside the whale.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r4.anchor: وروى عمران القطان عن الحسن قال والله ما كانت إلا صلاة أحدثها في بطن الحوت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r5.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r5.claim: The majority of scholars take it to mean Jonah’s glorification before the whale swallowed him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#2/r5.anchor: وجمهور العلماء على أنه أراد لولا ما تقدم له قبل التقام الحوت إياه من التسبيح

BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.claim: God told the fish Jonah was not its food but a trust in its belly, forbade breaking bone or severing a joint, and kept him there forty nights, as inferred from his being cast ashore sick.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.anchor: روي أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى السمكة أني لم أجعله لك رزقا ولكن جعلت بطنك له وعاء فلا تكسري منه عظما

BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.claim: Kashifi says three or seven days is also reported, while forty is better known; the fish crossed seven seas and Jonah's flesh and skin became transparent so he could see its wonders while remembering God.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (سه روز ياهفت روز اشهر آنست كه هل روز درشكم ماهى بود وآن ماهى هفت دريارا بكشت

BURSEVI:v7p380/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r3.claim: Jonah was among the glorifiers by praying inside the fish with the words of 21:87, or by frequent remembrance throughout his life.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r3.anchor: في بطن الحوت وهو قوله : {أن لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إنى كنت من الظالمين}

BURSEVI:v7p380/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r4.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v7p380/r4.claim: Sahl says the glorifiers are those who fulfilled God's rights before affliction through remembrance, prayer, or another act.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r4.anchor: وعن سهل من القائمين بحقوق الله قبل البلاء ذكرا أو صلاة أو غيرهما

BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.claim: Jonah's rescue because he glorified God urges abundant remembrance and magnifies its importance.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.anchor: فلم يلبث لكونه من المسبحين ، وفيه حث على إكثار الذكر وتعظيم لشأنه

BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.claim: When the heart is swallowed by the whale of the lower self, rescue comes through constant remembrance; turning to God in ease brings help in hardship, and good works support one who falls.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.anchor: وإشارة إلى أن خلاص يونس القلب إذا التقمه حوت النفس لا يكون إلا بملازمة ذكر الله

BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.speaker: الوسيط
BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.claim: Al-Wasit contrasts the remembering, righteous Jonah with forgetful, tyrannical Pharaoh, whose belief at drowning was rejected as too late.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.anchor: وفي الوسيط كان يونس عبدا صالحا ذاكرا

BURSEVI:v7p380/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r11.speaker: الشافعي
BURSEVI:v7p380/r11.claim: Al-Shafii says the best remedy for plague is glorification, because remembrance raises punishment and affliction, as this verse shows.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r11.anchor: وعن الشافعي أنفس ما يداوي به الطاعون التسبيح لأن الذكر يرفع العقوبة والعذاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.claim: Jonah's story was already recounted in Sura al-Anbiya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدمت قصة يونس، عليه السلام، في سورة الأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the view that Jonah's prior worship in times of ease saved him; Ibn Kathir says a later report supports it if sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.anchor: قاله الضحاك بن قيس، وأبو العالية، ووهب بن منبه، وقتادة، وغير واحد. واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says, 'Know God in ease and He will know you in hardship,' supporting remembrance before calamity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r2.anchor: وفي حديث عن ابن عباس: " تعرف إلى الله في الرخاء يعرفك في الشدة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك وعطاء بن السائب والسدي والحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and others interpret Jonah as one of those who prayed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، والضحاك، وعطاء بن السائب، والسدي، والحسن، وقتادة: {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} يعني: المصلين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r4.claim: Some specify that Jonah had been among those who prayed before the crisis.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r4.anchor: وصرح بعضهم بأنه كان من المصلين قبل ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r5.claim: Others say Jonah was among those who glorified God while still in his parents' wombs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: كان من المسبحين في جوف أبويه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others identify the glorification as Jonah's prayer in the darkness, quoted in 21:87–88, after which God answered and rescued him.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.claim: Anas, tentatively raising the report to the Prophet, says angels recognized Jonah's familiar prayer from a distant land; God recalled his accepted deeds and answered prayers in ease, then ordered the whale to cast him ashore.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.anchor: أنه سمع أنس بن مالك -ولا أعلم إلا أن أنسا يرفع الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم-

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah said, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r9.anchor: أحدها : من القائلين لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says it means Jonah prayed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r10.anchor: الثاني : من المصلين قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r11.speaker: وهب بن منبه
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r11.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says it means Jonah worshipped.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r11.anchor: من العابدين , قاله وهب بن منبه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r12.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r12.claim: Qutrub says it means Jonah repented.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r13.speaker: قيل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r13.claim: One saying is that he repented in ease, so God saved him from affliction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r13.anchor: وقيل تاب في الرخاء فنجاه الله من البلاء

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.claim: Water and wind challenged Jonah about fleeing, saying they worshipped the One worshipped in heaven and earth and feared His punishment; Jonah remembered his deeds until God inspired his call.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.anchor: أين أردت أن تهرب؟ من الذى يعبد فى السماء والأرض، فوالله إنا لنعبده

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r8.claim: Jonah called on God, declaring there is no god but Him, declaring Him pure and admitting he was among the wrongdoers.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r8.anchor: فنادى بالتوحيد، ثم نزه الرب عز وجل، أنه ليس أهل لأن يعصى، ثم اعترف، فقال:

MUQATIL:37:141-144/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r6.claim: Before his sin Jonah was among those who prayed; he was devoted to prayer and remembrance of God.
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r6.anchor: يعنى من المصلين قبل المعصية، وكان فى زمانه كثير الصلاة والذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r1.claim: The saved Jonah belonged to those who frequently remembered God with glorification.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r2.claim: Another explanation identifies the glorifiers as those who said, There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r2.anchor: أو من القائلين لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إنى كنت من الظالمين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r3.claim: A further explanation is that Jonah had been among those who prayed before this event.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every occurrence of tasbīḥ in the Qur'an means prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كل تسبيح فى القرآن فهو صلاة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r5.claim: A saying holds that a righteous deed lifts its doer when he stumbles.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#7/r5.anchor: ويقال أن العمل الصالح يرفع صاحبه إذا عثر

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r12.speaker: الكسائي والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r12.claim: Al-Kisai and al-Nahhas say the noun after anna is not kasra because the lām belongs to lawlā’s answer, not anna.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r12.anchor: قال الكسائي: لم تكسر «أن» لدخول اللام لأن اللام ليست لها. النحاس: والأمر كما قال

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r13.claim: Al-musabbiḥīn here means those who pray.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet through Abu Hurayra says God ordered the whale to take Yunus without injuring flesh or breaking bone; Yunus heard sea creatures’ glorification, prayed, and was rescued after angels interceded, then was cast ashore sick.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى ذكره حبس يونس في بطن الحوت أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن خذه

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r3.claim: Yunus’s prior praise and prayer caused his rescue, illustrating that a good deed can lift its doer after a fall.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r3.anchor: أخبر الله عز وجل أن يونس كان من المسبحين، وأن تسبيحه كان سبب نجاته

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-musabbiḥīn as those who prayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «من المسبحين» من المصلين

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r5.claim: Qatada says Yunus prayed beforehand for God’s protection, and God saved him.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r5.anchor: قال قتادة: كان يصلي قبل ذلك لحفظ الله عز وجل له فنجاه

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r7.claim: Muqatil takes the phrase to mean those who prayed and obeyed before the sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: «من المسبحين» من المصلين المطيعين قبل المعصية

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r8.speaker: وهب
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r8.claim: Wahb explains the phrase as “among the worshippers.”

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says Yunus did not pray inside the whale; God recalled good deeds he had stored in ease, which supported him in affliction.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما كان له صلاة في بطن الحوت ولكنه قدم عملا صالحا في حال الرخاء

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r10.claim: The author urges each servant to keep a private, sincere good deed hidden from people and stored for a day of need.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r10.anchor: ويحرص على خصلة من صالح عمله، يخلص فيها بينه وبين ربه

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r11.claim: The Prophet urged anyone able to keep a hidden good deed to do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r11.anchor: من استطاع منكم أن تكون له خبيئة من عمل صالح فليفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r12.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r12.claim: Bukhari and Muslim report from Ibn Umar that three people before Islam sheltered in a mountain cave during rain; a boulder blocked its entrance, so they invoked God by sincere good deeds to seek release.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r12.anchor: وقد خرج البخاري ومسلم من حديث ابن عمر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when Yunus uttered the supplication inside the whale, the whale cast him out.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r1.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: لما قال في بطن الحوت:

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that Yunus was among those who prayed inside the whale.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r2.anchor: وقيل: { من المسبحين } من المصلين في بطن الحوت

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r3.claim: The author prefers verbal glorification joined to the heart, supported by al-Tabari’s Abu Hurayra report that Yunus glorified in the whale and angels heard his voice.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r3.anchor: قلت: والأظهر أنه تسبيح اللسان الموافق للجنان، وعليه يدل حديث أبي هريرة المذكور قبل

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r4.claim: On the interpretation of verbal praise, kāna is an extra particle, yielding “unless he was among those who glorify.”
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r4.anchor: وتكون «كان» على هذا القول زائدة أي فلولا أنه من المسبحين

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r5.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas that the Prophet said no Muslim invokes Dhun-Nun’s supplication from the whale without receiving a response.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r5.anchor: وفي كتاب أبي داود عن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r6.claim: Yunus was a worshipper and one who prayed before entering the whale, and he also glorified God inside it.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r6.anchor: كان قبل مصليا مسبحا، وفي بطن الحوت كذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r7.claim: A report says the whale was told that Yunus was not made its food but that the whale was made his refuge and place of worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143/r7.anchor: وفي الخبر: فنودي الحوت: إنا لم نجعل يونس لك رزقا إنما جعلناك له حرزا ومسجدا

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.claim: IK and Ṭ say Jonah’s prior life of devotion prevented him from remaining in the fish until the Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.anchor: Had it not been for the life of devotion lived before these events, Jonah would have remained in the belly of the fish (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.claim: A Prophetic saying urges people to know God in ease, so God will aid them in difficulty.
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.anchor: a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, “Seek to know God in times of ease, and He will know you

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r3.speaker: Aj, IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r3.claim: Aj, IK, and Ṭ also understand the glorifiers as referring to Jonah’s prayer in the darkness, declaring God’s oneness and glorifying Him (21:87).
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r3.anchor: (21:87; Aj, IK, Ṭ); for the more extensive prayer and repentance of Jonah

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r4.claim: The commentary notes that Jonah’s prayer and repentance are more extensively related in the Biblical book of Jonah 2:1–9.
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r4.anchor: for the more extensive prayer and repentance of Jonah in the Bible, see Jonah 2:1–9

TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.claim: Jonah had worshipped and remembered God before the trial; God remembered him in distress and rescued him, instead of leaving him imprisoned in the whale until resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.anchor: ولكنه كان من الذاكرين الله قبل البلاء، فذكره الله في حال البلاء، فأنقذه ونجاه

TAB-FULL:v19p627/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r2.claim: Qatāda says Jonah prayed much in ease; a wisdom maxim says righteous deeds lift a person after a fall and give support when he is struck down.
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r2.anchor: قتادة {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} [الصافات: 143] " كان كثير الصلاة في الرخاء، فنجاه الله بذلك؛ قال: وقد كان يقال في الحكمة: إن العمل الصالح

TAB-FULL:v19p627/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r3.claim: Anas, with al-Ṭabarī unsure whether he raised it to the Prophet, reports that Jonah's prayer beneath the Throne was recognized; angels recalled his accepted deeds and answered prayers in ease, and God ordered the whale to cast him ashore.
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r3.anchor: سمعت أنس بن مالك، قال: ولا أعلم إلا أن أنسا يرفع الحديث إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v19p627/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “among those who glorify” as “among those who pray.”
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r4.anchor: ابن عباس {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} [الصافات: 143] قال: «من المصلين»

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, like Ibn ʿAbbās, interprets the phrase as referring to people who pray.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r1.anchor: سعيد بن جبير {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} [الصافات: 143] قال: «من المصلين»

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says Jonah had a righteous deed from his past.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r2.anchor: أبي العالية {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} [الصافات: 143] قال: «كان له عمل صالح فيما خلا»

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r3.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the phrase as “among those who pray.”

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.claim: In a sermon, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays urges people to remember God in ease so He remembers them in hardship, citing Jonah's remembrance and Pharaoh's failed belief at drowning.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.anchor: الضحاك بن قيس، يقول على منبره

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jonah's prayer was one he first performed inside the whale.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r5.anchor: الحسن، يقول في قوله: {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} [الصافات: 143] قال: «فوالله ما كانت إلا صلاة أحدثها في بطن الحوت»

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r6.claim: Qatāda rejects al-Ḥasan's view and says Jonah prayed often in ease.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r6.anchor: فذكرت ذلك لقتادة، فأنكر ذلك وقال: كان والله يكثر الصلاة في الرخاء

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r7.claim: Another reported view says the phrase refers to glorification, not prayer.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: كان ذلك تسبيحا، لا صلاة

SULAMI:v2p181#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r1.claim: Sahl reads the worshippers as those who fulfilled God's rights before the trial came.
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r1.anchor: قال سهل : من القائمين بحقوق الله قبل البلاء .

SULAMI:v2p181#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says Jonah's glorification alone could not save him; deliverance came only by divine grace and prior decree.
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : من العارفين أن تسبيحه لا ينجيه مما هو فيه وإنما ينجيه منه : الفضل وسابق القضاء .

SULAMI:v2p181#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r3.claim: Some take the worshippers as those who knew God in ease before hardship, in keeping with the Prophetic counsel to know God in prosperity.
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم في قوله ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين ﴾ أي من المتعرفين إلينا في الرخاء قبل الشدائد

SULAMI:v2p181#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r4.claim: The Prophet teaches that one who knows God in ease will find Him in hardship.
SULAMI:v2p181#3/r4.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' تعرف إلى الله في الرخاء يعرفك في الشدة ' .

TUSTARI:37:143/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:37:143/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:37:143/r1.claim: Jonah had been among those who fulfilled God's due before the affliction.
TUSTARI:37:143/r1.anchor: يعني من القائمين بحقوق الله تعالى قبل البلاء

TABATABAI:37:143-148/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r1.claim: The possibility that Jonah's glorification meant praise before the fish swallowed him is weak and should not be adopted.
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r1.anchor: فاحتمال كون المراد تسبيحه قبل التقام الحوت مرجوح لا ينبغي أن يصار إليه

TABATABAI:37:143-148/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r2.claim: Jonah's glorification declared God free of what his departure from his people and going away seemed to imply.
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r2.anchor: تسبيح له تعالى عما كان يشعر به فعله من ترك قومه وذهابه على وجهه

TABATABAI:37:143-148/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r3.claim: Of three views, the author prefers that Jonah glorified God specifically inside the fish; this glorification was the cause of his rescue from distress.
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r3.anchor: فالظاهر أن المراد بتسبيحه نداؤه في الظلمات

TABATABAI:37:143-148/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r4.claim: His call in the darkness begins by affirming that only God is truly worshipped, then declares Him free of the implication that Jonah had turned away toward another.
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r4.anchor: وقد قدم التهليل ليكون كالعلة المبينة لتسبيحه كأنه يقول لا معبود بالحق يتوجه إليه غيرك

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.claim: God preserved Jonah alive and well in the fish for days and nights; Jonah understood it as a trial for his action and called out in the fish's belly.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.anchor: حفظه حيا سويا في بطنه أياما وليالي ويونس عليه السلام يعلم أنها بلية ابتلاه الله بها

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r5.claim: God answered Jonah, ordered the fish to cast him ashore sick, and grew a gourd tree over him for shade.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r5.anchor: فاستجاب الله له فأمر الحوت أن يلفظه فنبذه بالعراء وهو سقيم فأنبت الله سبحانه عليه شجرة من يقطين

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.claim: Jonah's conduct displeased God and could not be ascribed to God's will; the trial made him acknowledge his own wrong and God's purity from willing such an act.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.anchor: فابتلاه الله بما ابتلاه ليعترف بظلمه على نفسه وأنه تعالى منزه عن إرادة مثله

TABRISI:37:142-147/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r10.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
TABRISI:37:142-147/r10.claim: Muqatil b. Hayyan says Jonah remained in the whale for three days.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r10.anchor: كانت ثلاثة أيام عن مقاتل بن حيان

TABRISI:37:142-147/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r11.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:37:142-147/r11.claim: ʿAtaʾ says Jonah remained in the whale for seven days.

TABRISI:37:142-147/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r12.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:37:142-147/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah remained in the whale for twenty days.

TABRISI:37:142-147/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r13.speaker: السدي، مقاتل بن سليمان، الكلبي
TABRISI:37:142-147/r13.claim: Al-Suddi, Muqatil b. Sulayman, and al-Kalbi say Jonah remained in the whale for forty days.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r13.anchor: وقيل: أربعين يوما عن السدي ومقاتل بن سليمان والكلبي

TABRISI:37:142-147/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:37:142-147/r14.claim: Qatada says Jonah had prayed in times of ease, so God rescued him in hardship.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r14.anchor: أي كان من المصلين في حال الرخاء فنجاه الله عند البلاء عن قتادة

TABRISI:37:142-147/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r15.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:37:142-147/r15.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr identifies Jonah’s praise as his prayer, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.”
TABRISI:37:142-147/r15.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير. وقيل: من المسبحين أي من

TABRISI:37:142-147/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:142-147/r16.claim: The phrase may also mean those who declare God free of what is unfitting to His nature and remember Him.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r16.anchor: من المسبحين أي من المنزهين لله عما لا يليق به ولا يجوز في صفته

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#6/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#6/r1.claim: An alternative reported sense of al-musabbiḥīn is those who pray.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#6/r1.anchor: فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} يقال: من المصلين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.claim: Mujahid says Jonah's frequent prayer and remembrance in ease spared him from remaining in the whale as punishment until resurrection; al-Kalbi agrees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: فلولا أنه كان في الرخاء قبل أن يلتقمه الحوت، {من المسبحين} يعني المصلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r2.speaker: أبو زيد عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r2.claim: Abu Zayd reports Ibn Abbas's explanation that the glorifiers are those who pray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r2.anchor: وروى أبو زيد عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من المسبحين} من المصلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r3.claim: Qatada says Jonah used to pray frequently in times of ease.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان يكثر الصلاة في الرخاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.claim: Al-Rabi b. Anas says that without Jonah's righteous deeds he would have remained in the whale.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: كان خلاله عمل صالح للبث في بطنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak b. Qays urges remembrance in ease so God remembers one in hardship, contrasting Jonah with Pharaoh, who remembered only while drowning and was rebuked.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك بن قيس (¬3) (¬4): اذكروا الله في الرخاء يذكركم في الشدة، فإن يونس كان عبدا صالحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r6.claim: Qatada says a righteous deed raises its doer, so whenever the person stumbles, he finds support.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة في الحكمة: إن العمل الصالح يرفع صاحبه كلما عثر وجد متكئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r11.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r11.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas's alternative view that Jonah glorified God while inside the whale.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r11.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من المسبحين} قال: يريد في بطن الحوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r12.claim: Said b. Jubayr identifies Jonah's glorification as his prayer, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers,” spoken in the whale, unlike the view that he prayed beforehand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r12.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: يعني قوله: {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين} [الأنبياء: 87]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah did not pray inside the whale but had already done good; he remained only a short time and was expelled well after being swallowed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.anchor: قال الحسن: ما كانت له صلاة في بطن الحوت ولكنه قدم عملا صالحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that angels heard Jonah's faint glorification, recalled his past good deeds, interceded, and God ordered the whale to cast him onto shore.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r5.claim: Jonah had been among those who prayed before this event.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r5.anchor: فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين } من المصلين قبل ذلك

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r2.claim: With an answer, لولا marks a condition whose result would occur but for another circumstance: Jonah would have remained until resurrection but for glorifying God.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r2.anchor: فإذا رأيت للولا جوابا فليست بهذا المعنى، كقوله:

ELMALILI:37:139-179/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r5.claim: The translation makes his being among those who glorify God frequently the condition that prevented the following outcome.
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r5.anchor: Eğer çok tesbih edenlerden olmasa idi

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.claim: Alusi transmits the People of the Book's account: sent to Nineveh, overwhelmed by its wickedness, Yunus fled toward Tarshish via Jaffa and boarded a ship caught in a storm.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.anchor: Âlûsî tefsirinde der ki: “Yûnus aleyhisselâm hakkında ehl-i kitâbın kitaplarında mezkur olan şudur

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r16.claim: Yunus was already among those who frequently glorified God; in the darkness he called, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.”
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r16.anchor: öteden beri Allah’ı tesbih ile çok zikrederdi, bu zulümâtta da لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.claim: These verses briefly report what befell Jonah after he left his homeland; the Qur’an foregrounds the story’s instructive lesson rather than supplying bare history.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.anchor: Kur’an’ın amacı, salt tarihî bilgi vermek değil, olayın ibret verici yönünü öne çıkarmak olduğu için onun hayatı hakkında daha fazla ayrıntı vermeye gerek görülmemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.speaker: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.claim: The Bible’s fuller account broadly matches the Qur’an: sent to warn Nineveh, Jonah flees by ship toward Tarshish, is cast overboard by lot in a storm and swallowed; after prayer he is returned ashore, recommissioned, and Nineveh repents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.anchor: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’te Hz. Yûnus hakkında genel hatlarıyla Kur’an’da verilenlerle de uyuşan daha ayrıntılı bilgi bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.claim: God used extraordinary events to train prophets for difficult struggles for monotheism; Jonah’s story illustrates that prophetic preparation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.anchor: Allah Teâlâ peygamberlerini, başlarına gelen olağan dışı olaylarla eğitmiş, zorlu geçecek bir tevhid mücadelesine hazırlamıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r11.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r11.claim: Tabari says Jonah was rescued through the fish because before the calamity he had diligently fulfilled his duties of worship to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r11.anchor: Taberî, 143. âyete dayanarak Yûnus’un, bu musibet başına gelmezden önce Allah’a karşı kulluk görevlerini titizlikle uygulamış olması sayesinde balık vasıtasıyla kurtarıldığını belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.claim: The counterfactual means that without being a good servant, Jonah would have died inside the fish and remained there until resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.anchor: yani o, iyi bir kul olmasaydı balık kendisini yutacak, orada ölecek ve tekrar dirilmesi kıyamete kalacaktı.

BURHAN:v4p379/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p379/r1.speaker: ابن الشجري
BURHAN:v4p379/r1.claim: Ibn al-Shajari objects that substitution is the strongest parsing for an exception after negation, though accusative is allowed; its use in both verses suggests a positive construction, answered by the author's point that negation is implicit.
BURHAN:v4p379/r1.anchor: وقال ابن الشجري هذا يخالف أصح الإعرابين لأن المستثنى بعد النفي يقوى فيه البدل

BURHAN:v4p379/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p379/r3.speaker: الخليل
BURHAN:v4p379/r3.claim: Ibn Barjan quotes al-Khalil that Qur'anic لولا means هلا except in Jonah's case, where its answer differs; the author questions this exception.
BURHAN:v4p379/r3.anchor: ونقل ابن برجان في تفسيره في أواخر سورة هود عن الخليل إن جميع ما في القرآن من لولا

ITQAN:v2p511/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p511/r1.speaker: الخليل
ITQAN:v2p511/r1.claim: Al-Khalil is reported to say that every Qur'anic lawlā means halā except 37:143, but Suyuti questions this generalization in light of other verses.
ITQAN:v2p511/r1.anchor: نقل عن الخليل أن جميع ما في القرآن من لولا فهي بمعنى هلا إلا ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين ﴾ وفيه نظر

ITQAN:v2p511/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p511/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p511/r2.claim: In 12:24, lawlā is conditional with an omitted answer meaning he would have desired or approached her; two other conditional uses likewise have omitted answers.
ITQAN:v2p511/r2.anchor: لولا فيه امتناعية وجوابها محذوف أي لهم بها أو لواقعها

ITQAN:v2p511/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p511/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
ITQAN:v2p511/r3.claim: Abu Malik, via al-Suddi, says every Qur'anic lawlā means fahalā except 10:98 and 37:143; Suyuti says this clarifies that al-Khalil meant lawlā prefixed by fa.
ITQAN:v2p511/r3.anchor: قال كل ما في القرآن فلولا فهو فهلا إلا حرفين في يونس ﴿ فلولا كانت قرية آمنت فنفعها إيمانها ﴾

NAHHAS:v3p438/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r11.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p438/r11.claim: Al-Kisa'i says the lām is not a governor of أن; al-Nahhas agrees it is the answer to لولا.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r11.anchor: قال الكسائي لم يكسر أن لدخول اللام لأن اللام ليست لها قال أبو جعفر والأمر كما قال

NAHHAS:v3p438/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v3p438/r12.claim: Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas explain the worshippers as those who prayed.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r12.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود وابن عباس فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين قالا أي من المصلين

NAHHAS:v3p438/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r13.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v3p438/r13.claim: Qatada says Jonah prayed beforehand, and God preserved that prior worship and rescued him.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r13.anchor: قال قتادة كان يصلي قبل ذلك فحفظ الله جل وعز له ذلك فنجاه

NAHHAS:v3p438/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r14.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
NAHHAS:v3p438/r14.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says Jonah had done righteous deeds beforehand.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r14.anchor: قال الربيع بن أنس لولا أنه كان قبل ذلك له عمل صالح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.claim: Jonah’s being among those who glorified God prevented his remaining in the fish until resurrection; this is another original conditional use of lولا.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.anchor: وفي الصافات : ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين للبث

BURHAN:v4p375/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p375/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p375/r6.claim: The predicate after لولا is omitted and supplied by its response; affirmative responses usually take لام, though it can be understood without it.
BURHAN:v4p375/r6.anchor: ويلزم في خبرها الحذف ويستغنى بجوابها عن الخبر والأكثر في جوابها المثبت اللام

BURHAN:v2p134/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p134/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p134/r4.claim: The people’s request for Moses’ prayer and Jonah’s deliverance are connected with teachings about divine relief, followed by the cave companions’ appeal through their best deeds.
BURHAN:v2p134/r4.anchor: وفى هذا بين صلى الله عليه وسلم أصحاب الغار الثلاثة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.claim: The descriptive form marks a settled trait: Yunus was rescued from distress through his sustained practice of glorification.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.anchor: والمجيء بالصيغة الوصفية هنا إشارة إلى أن مداومة التسبيح تخلِّص من الكروب والمكاره، وأن يونس إنما نجا من هذه الشدة بمداومة التسبيح
